*** SPRINT 75 / V0.29.30: 6 of 11 closed, 5 PASSING (US-561, US-563, US-564, US-565, US-566), 1 blocked-by-hardware (US-560/BL-034). THE V0.29 CLOSEOUT LINE IS DONE except US-560. NEXT ITERATION PICKS UP THE F-132 CHROME STORIES: US-555 (top bar 3-column grid), then 556/557/558/559. ***

*** US-565 CLOSED passes:true -- magnetometer acquisition. Full AC-by-AC detail in sprint.json completionNotes; reusable lessons below. ***

*** READ THIS BEFORE US-555/556/557 -- IT IS STILL LIVE AND IT IS NOT MINE, IT IS FROM THE US-560 ITERATION: the chromium kiosk runs with NO --window-size and NO --force-device-scale-factor, so the dashboard renders into a 1280x720 CSS-pixel viewport, while US-557's band budget ('body 224px; 3 rows + footer = 222') is ~320-canvas arithmetic. Budgeted against one canvas, rendered on another. If 555/556/557 are built and IN-CAR-validated at 720p, settling BL-034 afterwards silently invalidates all three. Flag it to PM again before starting; do not silently pick a canvas. ***

**THE STORY'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND FINDING THAT OUT WAS THE WORK.** US-565 said 'the lever is CNTL2'. It is not: the chip ALREADY read back 0x08 (continuous 100 Hz) before I changed anything, and a VERIFIED write of 10 Hz changed the latch not at all. The real fault was the ICM-20948's cyclic slave0 shadow readout doing ONE transfer and stopping. **When a story hands you a named lever, measure the lever's CURRENT STATE FIRST.** One read of CNTL2 before touching anything would have redirected the whole investigation, and it is the cheapest possible measurement.

**MY OWN FIRST PROBE RUN WAS INVALID AND I ALMOST SHIPPED ITS NUMBERS.** I swept 8 CNTL2 levers and got a clean-looking table. Every row was garbage: the readback column said 'slave4 transfer did not finish' on all 8, which meant the WRITES on that same path had not landed either -- I had measured 8 variations of doing nothing. I only caught it because I printed the readback next to the result. **Atlas's earlier rate sweep (100Hz->zeros, 10Hz->latched, 50Hz->partial) has the same defect and should be treated as noise, not evidence.** Root cause: slave4 does not complete while the cyclic slave0 readout is running, and the adafruit driver only gets away with it because it does all its slave4 work during init, BEFORE enabling slave0. **A probe that cannot report its own failure is not a measurement. Print the verification column even when you are sure.**

**TWO CANDIDATE FAULTS CAN LOOK IDENTICAL FROM THE CONSUMER SIDE -- FIND A DIFFERENT DATA PATH.** 'Chip stopped converting' and 'chip is fine, transfer stopped' both present as a frozen dev.magnetic. Reading the measurement registers over a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT path (slave4, shadow quiesced) settled it in one command: the chip was converting and dithering the whole time. Same trick is available whenever a value is frozen -- ask the source directly instead of theorising about the pipe.

**CHANGE-INDEX BEATS DISTINCT-COUNT FOR DIAGNOSING A FREEZE.** '2 distinct values' means something completely different if both changes land in the first second than if they are spread over the window. Recording WHERE the changes fall turned an ambiguous count into 'one transfer at init, then nothing' -- the actual diagnosis. Cheap to add, and I would not have got there without it.

**MAKE THE FAKE MODEL THE FAILURE MODE, NOT JUST THE INTERFACE.** The AK09916 only loads a new measurement once a read reaches ST2. My FakeAk09916 implements that rule, so shortening the burst to a 'tidier' 6-byte data read makes the suite go RED. I VERIFIED that rather than asserting it: 9-byte frame -> 8 distinct of 8; 6-byte frame -> 1 of 8. A fake that always serves fresh data scores the broken driver and the fixed one identically -- which is how the original defect survived a green suite for months.

**EXTRACT A DEGRADE PATH OUT OF '# pragma: no cover' GLUE SO IT CAN BE TESTED.** 'A magnetometer fault must not cost accel and gyro' was a try/except inside hardware-only code, i.e. an inert guard -- present, unenforced. Pulling it into _attachDirectMagnetometer(icm, bus, bypassFactory) made it three parametrised tests. Small refactor, and it converts a comment into a guarantee.

**VERIFY CONFIG BY READBACK.** The whole root cause upstream is that the driver writes CNTL2, discards the completion flag its OWN helper returns, and never reads back. Anything you write to hardware, read back and compare -- and treat a discarded return value from a hardware write as a defect on sight.

**THE PI IS REACHABLE AND HARDWARE CHARACTERIZATION IS IN-BUDGET.** ssh chi-eclipse-01, venv at ~/obd2-venv/bin/python, passwordless sudo. **ALWAYS stop eclipse-obd before touching I2C** (the ICM is bank-switched; two processes corrupt each other -- Atlas wedged the bus this way with a read-only command) and **ALWAYS restart it under a shell `trap ... EXIT`** so a crash mid-probe cannot leave the car's capture service down. The Pi DB is locked by the running service: use sqlite3 with `file:...?mode=ro` via python, not the sqlite3 CLI (its nolock URI is rejected).

ENVIRONMENT (re-confirmed + one correction): `python -m pytest <paths>` prints the summary without `-q`. `python -m ruff check --output-format=concise <files>` gives one line per finding -- much better than the default when you just want the codes. **CORRECTION TO A PRIOR NOTE: the PowerShell tool does NOT support heredocs (`<<'PY'` is a parser error).** For a multi-line python script, Write it to a temp file and run it, then delete it -- which is also how I edited sprint.json safely. **Always `json.load()` sprint.json after editing and print the story list + a spot-check key; my scoped diff was 25+/7-, and the only non-US-565 removal was a stray comma.** Index lock CLEAR all session.
